items.title: Ep37. How are electric car engines different from petrol car engines?
items.desc: In this episode, Lily and Max look under the bonnet to discover how electric cars are different from petrol cars. They explore how petrol engines use tiny controlled bursts, why diesel engines don’t need spark plugs, and how electric motors use batteries and magnetic forces to turn the wheels. They also uncover how hybrid cars combine fuel and electricity, how regenerative braking puts energy back into a battery, and the advantages and disadvantages of each type of car.

items.title: Ep36. How do seeds grow?
items.desc: In this episode, Lily and Max discover how a tiny seed grows into a whole plant! They peek inside a seed to find the baby plant waiting within, learn what wakes a sleeping seed, and explore how roots know to grow down while shoots reach up toward the light. They also investigate how a delicate shoot pushes through soil, and what happens when a seed doesn’t get the water, warmth or oxygen it needs.

items.title: Ep35. Why is Venus the hottest planet?
items.desc: In this scorching episode, Lily and Max discover how Venus’s thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat like an enormous blanket. They also explore Venus’s backwards spin, find out why one Venusian rotation is longer than its year, and learn how scientists use radar to see through its mysterious clouds.

items.title: Ep34. Why do spoons flip your face reflection?
items.desc: In this episode, Lily and Max investigate how shiny spoons reflect light, discover the difference between convex and concave surfaces, and learn why moving a spoon closer can suddenly flip your reflection again. With a light-ray race, funny stretched faces and an easy experiment to try at home, an ordinary spoon becomes a tiny science laboratory!

items.title: Ep33. I keep telling myself I can do something, will I get better at It?
items.desc: In this episode, Lily and Max explore the surprising power of self-talk and why positive words work best when they’re followed by practice and action.
